Usage: canvasnet info <input> [--page N | --all-pages] [--json]

Reads only the file header: the format, the pixel size, the channels, whether it has transparency,
the number of frames of a GIF, and the EXIF orientation of a JPEG. An SVG reports its intrinsic size.
A PDF, PPTX, or VSDX document reports its number of pages and the size of a page (the first, or the
one chosen with --page, or every page with --all-pages): in pixels at 96 dpi and in points, the
rotation of a PDF page, and the name of a VSDX page. An OpenSCAD model is parsed (not evaluated) and
reports the modules and functions it defines and its include and use directives.

Examples:
  canvasnet info photo.jpg
  canvasnet info report.pdf --all-pages
  canvasnet info part.scad --json
  canvasnet info drawing.svg --json

Show the format, size, and properties of an image or drawing without rendering it

Options:
  --page <N>   For a document, describe this page or slide, counted from 1 (default 1)
  --all-pages  For a document, describe every page or slide

Usage: canvasnet render <input> -o <output> [options]

Reads PNG, JPEG, BMP, TIFF, GIF, JPEG 2000, SVG, PDF, PPTX, VSDX, or SCAD and writes the format of the output
extension. Vector sources are flattened over white; a JPEG is turned upright by its EXIF orientation.
A PDF page, PPTX slide, or VSDX page is 96 dpi by default; choose it with --page and the size with --dpi.
An OpenSCAD model is drawn from one viewpoint (--view, --azimuth, --elevation, --projection) at 800x800
pixels unless a size is given; -D sets its variables. Its include and use directives are read from the
folder of the model and below it only, and one that names a missing file is an error.
The operations --crop, --resize, --fit, --rotate, --flip, --pad, and the photo tools --grayscale, --invert,
--threshold, --levels, --brightness, --contrast, --auto-levels, --deskew, --trim, and --grid (repeatable) are
applied in the order written, after the source is loaded and sized; crop, resize, rotate, flip, and pad are
commands of their own. --rotate takes any angle; --deskew and --json report the tilt that was found.

Examples:
  canvasnet render drawing.svg -o drawing.png
  canvasnet render drawing.svg --width 1200 -o drawing.png
  canvasnet render report.pdf --page 2 --dpi 150 -o page2.png
  canvasnet render slides.pptx --all-pages -o out/slide-{page}.png
  canvasnet render part.scad --view top -D width=30 -o part-top.png
  canvasnet render part.scad --azimuth 30 --elevation 20 --projection perspective -o part.png
  canvasnet render photo.jpg --crop 10%,10%,80%,80% --resize 800x600 -o small.png
  canvasnet render logo.png --fit 256x256 --pad 8 --pad-color white -o icon.png
  canvasnet render napkin.jpg --fit 2048x2048 --auto-levels --deskew --trim -o sketch.png --json
  canvasnet render sketch.png --grayscale --threshold auto -o bw.png
  canvasnet render sketch.png --grid 100 -o sketch-grid.png
  canvasnet render shot.png -o shot.jpg --quality 85
[truncated]

Usage: canvasnet crop <input> <geometry> -o <output> [options]

Cuts out the rectangle x,y,w,h or WxH+X+Y (origin and size), each value in pixels (10 or 10px) or percent (10%).
A part that lies outside the image is cut off at its edge; a rectangle that starts outside the image is an error.
'crop' is 'render' with this one operation first, so it takes every option of render (--page, --dpi,
--background, --format, --quality, --no-clobber, --json, ...). The operations given as options
(--crop, --resize, --fit, --rotate, --flip, --pad, --grayscale, --threshold, --deskew, --trim, --grid, ...)
are applied after it, in the order written.

Examples:
  canvasnet crop photo.png 10,10,200,100 -o part.png
  canvasnet crop photo.png 200x100+10+10 -o part.png
  canvasnet crop slide.pdf 0,0,50%,100% --page 2 --dpi 150 -o left-half.png

Cut a rectangle out of an image, drawing, or document page

Options:
  --page <N>                      The page or slide to render, counted from 1 (default 1)
  --all-pages                     Render every page or slide; the output must contain {page} or be a directory
  --dpi <D>                       Resolution of a PDF, PPTX, or VSDX page in dots per inch (default 96; VSDX needs a whole number)
  --scale <factor>                Multiply the natural size by a factor, for example 2 or 0.5
  --width <pixels>                Target width in pixels; the height keeps the aspect ratio unless --height is given
  --height <pixels>               Target height in pixels; the width keeps the aspect ratio unless --width is given
  --size <WxH>                    Exact target size, for example 800x600 (shorthand for --width and --height)
  --background <color>            Color to flatten transparency over: white (default for vector sources), black, #RRGGBB, #RRGGBBAA, transparent
  --no-auto-orient                Do not turn a JPEG upright according to its EXIF orientation
  --strict                   
[truncated]

Usage: canvasnet rotate <input> <degrees> -o <output> [options]

Rotates clockwise by the angle in degrees (-90 is 270, 3.5 or -3.5 level a slightly tilted scan).
A multiple of 90 degrees is an exact pixel move; any other angle grows the canvas to hold the whole image
and fills the corners with --rotate-fill (default: the --background, else white for an opaque image, else transparent).
'rotate' is 'render' with this one operation first, so it takes every option of render (--page, --dpi,
--background, --format, --quality, --no-clobber, --json, ...). The operations given as options
(--crop, --resize, --fit, --rotate, --flip, --pad, --grayscale, --threshold, --deskew, --trim, --grid, ...)
are applied after it, in the order written.

Examples:
  canvasnet rotate scan.png 90 -o upright.png
  canvasnet rotate scan.png -3.5 --rotate-fill white -o level.png
  canvasnet rotate scan.jpg 180 -o flipped.jpg --quality 85

Usage: canvasnet compare <a> <b> [options]

Reads two images, drawings, or document pages like 'render' and reports how much they differ: the mean
absolute error (MAE), the root mean square error (RMSE), the peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), the structural
similarity (SSIM), the fraction of pixels that differ by more than --tolerance, and the error of each cell of
a grid, so that you can see where the images differ. The inputs must have the same size: use --resize-to a,
b, or WxH to bring them to one; a vector input is rendered at that size.
--diff, --side-by-side, and --overlay write pictures of the differences. --threshold makes the command fail
with exit code 1 (after writing the result and the pictures) when a metric is not within its limit.
--page, --dpi, and the SCAD options apply to both inputs; --a-page, --b-page, --a-dpi, --b-dpi, --a-view,
--b-view, --a-define, and --b-define apply to one input and win.

Examples:
  canvasnet compare reference.png redraw.png
  canvasnet compare reference.png redraw.svg --resize-to a --diff diff.png
  canvasnet compare reference.png redraw.svg --resize-to a --grid 4x4 --side-by-side cmp.png --threshold ssim=0.9 --json
  canvasnet compare deck.pptx deck.pdf --a-page 2 --b-page 2 --resize-to a --overlay blend.png
  canvasnet compare sketch.jpg model.scad --b-view front --resize-to a --overlay blend.png

Usage: canvasnet montage <inputs...> -o <output> [options]

Reads images, drawings, or document pages like 'render' and writes one contact sheet with a cell for each,
in the order given, row by row. A document contributes its --page (the first by default), or every page
with --all-pages. Each image is fitted into a --cell (256x256 by default; a vector input is rendered at the
cell size) and --labels writes its file name below it. The sheet is at most 8192 pixels on a side.

Examples:
  canvasnet montage a.png b.png c.png -o sheet.png
  canvasnet montage deck.pptx --all-pages --labels -o deck-sheet.png
  canvasnet montage *.png --columns 4 --cell 200x150 --background #333333 --labels -o gallery.png
  canvasnet montage report.pdf part.scad logo.svg --labels -o overview.jpg --json

Compose images and document pages into one contact sheet, optionally labeled

Options:
  -o, --output <file>        The file the contact sheet is written to; its extension selects the format
  --columns <N>              Number of columns, 1-64 (default: as square as possible)
  --cell <WxH>               Size of the image area of each cell (default 256x256, each side at least 16)
  --fit <mode>               How an image is fitted into its cell: contain (default; keeps the aspect ratio) or stretch
  --spacing <N>              Space between cells in pixels (default 8)
  --padding <N>              Space around the sheet in pixels (default 8)
  --background <color>       Opaque color of the sheet: white (default), black, #RRGGBB, or a color name
  --labels                   Write the file name (and the page of a document) below each cell
  --page <N>                 The page or slide to render, counted from 1 (default 1)
  --all-pages                Add every page or slide of a document, in order, instead of one
  --dpi <D>                  Resolution of a PDF, PPTX, or VSDX page in dots per inch (default 96; VSDX needs a whole number)

Usage: canvasnet inspect colors <input> [--count N] [options]
canvasnet inspect pixel <input> <x,y> [--radius R] [options]

Reads an image, drawing, or document page like 'render', applies the same operations (--crop, --deskew,
--auto-levels, ... in the order written), and reports what the pixels contain; no file is written.
colors reports the dominant colors (shades within about 32 levels are one color) with their share of the
pixels, and the luma statistics (mean, range, percentiles, the level --threshold auto would choose, and a
16-bin histogram) that help to choose --levels and --threshold values. pixel reports the color and luma of
one pixel; with --radius also the pixels around it and their mean. Coordinates are those of the image after
the operations, from 0,0 at the top left. Transparent pixels are flattened over the --background (white by
default) before they are counted.

Examples:
  canvasnet inspect colors napkin.jpg --count 6
  canvasnet inspect colors photo.jpg --crop 100,100,50,50 --json
  canvasnet inspect pixel sketch.png 412,230
  canvasnet inspect pixel sketch.png 412,230 --radius 2 --json
